description:
We don’t just observe Earth — we turn its data into action. 🌍🚀
A team built to challenge the limits, solve real problems, and transform NASA data into the future of resilient agriculture. Let’s build. Let’s compete. Let’s make an impact.
summary: OASIS 51 is a bilingual (Arabic and English) web app that helps farmers in Oman choose crop rotations with limited water. The farmer marks the farm on a map and enters the area, available water, irrigation method, optional salinity tests, the previous crop and a priority. Using 10 years of NASA POWER daily data and FAO-56 methods, OASIS 51 estimates crop water demand and compares a reference rotation with two alternatives over two seasons. It shows the water balance, heat and salinity risks, what-if scenarios and the sources behind each result. Results are planning estimates for local checking.
details:
What it does: compares three crop rotations for a farm in Oman and shows water needs, risks and the reasons behind each plan, in Arabic and English.

How it works: NASA POWER daily data (2016-2025) -> FAO-56 Penman-Monteith evapotranspiration -> crop water demand (FAO-56 crop coefficients, FAO-29 salinity) -> a rule engine that checks 42 two-season sequences and ranks them by the farmer's priority. Scenarios test less water or hotter conditions.

Benefits: farmers see in seconds whether their water is enough for each plan. Missing data stays 'unknown' instead of zero, and every result shows its source.

Tools: Next.js, React, TypeScript, Leaflet, Recharts, Python, FastAPI. Code (MIT): https://github.com/3oman/OASIS51
